desc:
Given an integer array nums and an integer m, count the contiguous blocks of length exactly m that contain every number from 1 to m exactly once (in any order). Other values, repeated values or missing values make a block invalid.

nums = [2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 3, 3, 1], m = 3
[2,1,3] ok   [1,3,1] no   [3,1,2] ok
[1,2,3] ok   [2,3,3] no   [3,3,1] no
result = 3
hints: Sorting each block and comparing it with [1, 2, ..., m] works but is O(n · m log m).
A block of length m is a permutation of 1..m exactly when each of the m values 1..m occurs exactly once in it.
Keep a count per value and a number good = how many values in 1..m currently have count exactly 1. The block is valid when good == m.
editorial: Because the block has exactly m elements, it is a permutation of 1..m precisely when all m values in the range 1..m each appear exactly once. Maintain a hash map of counts for the current window and the number good of values in 1..m whose count is exactly 1.

When a value in 1..m enters, its count goes 0 → 1 (good + 1), or 1 → 2 (good - 1), and nothing changes at higher counts. When it leaves, the changes are reversed (1 → 0 loses one, 2 → 1 gains one). Values outside 1..m are simply ignored by good. Count the windows where good == m. O(n) time, O(m) space.
